title: Finite stratified oriented products form a coherent conservative cover
statement:
Let $S$ be Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $f:X\to S$ be of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $X=\coprod_\alpha X_\alpha$ and $S=\coprod_\beta S_\beta$ be finite constructible stratifications [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset], with stratum immersions $i_\alpha:X_\alpha\to X$ and $j_\beta:S_\beta\to S$. Form
$$P_{\alpha\beta}=(X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow{\times}_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(S_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}$$
by [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] for $fi_\alpha$ and $j_\beta$, and let $V_f=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow{\times}_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. If $p_1,p_2,\tau$ are the projections and structural $2$-morphism of $P_{\alpha\beta}$, the triple $(i_\alpha p_1,j_\beta p_2,\tau)$ gives $u_{\alpha\beta}:P_{\alpha\beta}\to V_f$ by the same universal property. Let $u:\coprod_{\alpha,\beta}P_{\alpha\beta}\to V_f$ be the induced geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] from the finite coproduct topos, with the construction and inverse image $u^{-1}A=(u_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}A)_{\alpha\beta}$ of [lem-trf-finite-coproduct-topos-coherent]. Then $u$ is coherent and conservative [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Author draft §8.1, printed p. 17, converse coherence argument via the finite coproduct of stratum oriented products; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Finite presentation implies finite type: a finitely presented algebra has a finite set of algebra generators. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. For any stratum $Z$ of $X$ or $S$, its immersion factors as a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow O$ into an open subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The open $O$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The closed immersion is of finite type: over each affine it is $R\to R/I$, an algebra generated by the image of $1$, and its affine source over that affine is quasi-compact. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] again makes $Z$ Noetherian. Consequently $X,S,X_\alpha,S_\beta$ are quasi-compact and are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); open-subscheme input: properties.tex 01OW/01OZ; the quotient-algebra finite-type calculation is written out.

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], a morphism with quasi-compact source and quasi-separated target is quasi-compact, and a morphism with quasi-separated source is quasi-separated. Step 1 therefore verifies these properties for $f$, $fi_\alpha$ and $j_\beta$. Apply [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation] to $X\to S\leftarrow S$ and $X_\alpha\to S\leftarrow S_\beta$, obtaining small finite-limit sites for $V_f$ and $P_{\alpha\beta}$. Their topologies are generated by finite families of types (a),(b) and singleton families of type (c). The pretopology generated by these families still has finite families: base changes preserve the generating types, and any finite successive composition has a finite union of finite index sets. This is the finite-family pretopology described in ILO XI 2.5. Thus [lem-trf-finitary-site-coherent-generators] applies and makes $V_f$ and every $P_{\alpha\beta}$ coherent, with coherent associated representables $H_Z$.

source.place: Proof of XI Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 178–179, PDF pp. 184–185; Cov(Z) and stability of the three generating types under base change.

proof.text:
There are finitely many pairs $(\alpha,\beta)$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-coproduct-topos-coherent] to the coherent components from step 2: the source $\mathcal E=\coprod_{\alpha,\beta}P_{\alpha\beta}$ is a coherent topos, and coherence of an object in it is componentwise. For a triple $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ on the target site, the base-change clause of [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation], with $a=i_\alpha$, $b=1_S$, $d=j_\beta$, gives
$$u_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}H_Z\simeq H_{Z_{\alpha\beta}},\qquad Z_{\alpha\beta}=(U\times_X X_\alpha\to V\leftarrow W\times_S S_\beta).$$
This is an associated representable of the component site, hence coherent by step 2. The coproduct formula identifies $u^{-1}H_Z$ with precisely this tuple, so it is coherent. Both source and target are now coherent, and the morphism criterion in [lem-trf-finitary-site-coherent-generators] shows that $u^{-1}$ preserves every coherent object. This proves coherence of $u$ in [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: XI 1.6, 1.9 and proof of Lemma 2.5, applied to the finite stratified family; the finite-coproduct input is isolated separately.

proof.text: The target finite-cover site of step 2 has enough points for sheaves of sets by [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points]. Fix any point $z:\mathbf{Set}\to V_f$. Its two projections are points of $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, so [lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric] represents them by geometric points $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_x\to X$ and $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_y\to S$. Conjugate the structural $2$-morphism of $z$ by these point isomorphisms, obtaining $c:y\Rightarrow f(x)$. Apply the uniqueness clause of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] with source $\mathbf{Set}$: it identifies $z$ with the point classified by $(x,y,c)$, including its structural arrow. This derives the all-points-as-triples assertion from that universal property, without taking it from the module-conservativity statement.

source.place: XI 1.4 and 1.8, printed pp. 172–174; Stacks sites.tex 00YQ (proposition-criterion-points), etale-cohomology.tex 04HU (lemma-points-small-etale-site).

proof.text: Choose the unique strata containing the images of $x$ and $y$ using [def-constructible-stratification]. A geometric point factors through its chosen stratum as a scheme morphism, not just set-theoretically: factor the stratum immersion through an open $O$ as in [def-weil-closed-immersion]; the point first factors through $O$. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset O$, let $I$ define the closed stratum and let $\mathfrak p$ be the kernel of $R\to\Omega$. Containment of the image point says $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so this map factors through $R/I$. This gives geometric points $x_\alpha$ and $y_\beta$ on the strata with the same algebraically closed fields. The reducedness of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ kills the defining ideal; no reducedness assumption on the stratum is needed. The canonical set-stalk bijections in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied to the two stratum immersions, identify the composite point functors with $x,y$; their germ formulas make these identifications natural in the set sheaf. Thus the structural arrow is the same arrow $c:j_\beta y_\beta\Rightarrow fi_\alpha x_\alpha$. The existence clause of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] yields $z_{\alpha\beta}:\mathbf{Set}\to P_{\alpha\beta}$; its uniqueness clause gives $u_{\alpha\beta}z_{\alpha\beta}\simeq z$. Composing with the component inclusion supplied by [lem-trf-finite-coproduct-topos-coherent] lifts $z$ to the source of $u$.

source.place: XI 1.4, 1.8–1.9; stratum factorization is the displayed affine quotient calculation (Stacks morphisms.tex 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Let $a:F\to G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on $V_f$ for which $u^{-1}a$ is invertible. For every point $z$ in the conservative family of step 4, take its lift $\widetilde z$ from step 5. The isomorphism $u\widetilde z\simeq z$ and composition of inverse images [def-trf-geometric-morphism] give $z^{-1}a\simeq\widetilde z^{-1}u^{-1}a$, which is invertible. Apply [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points] to conclude that $a$ is invertible. Thus $u^{-1}$ reflects isomorphisms of set sheaves, exactly conservativity in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Empty components contribute no points; if there is no point to test, the enough-points theorem still asserts reflection by its possibly empty family. Together with step 3 this proves the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 00YQ (proposition-criterion-points); the lifted-point inverse-image composition is XI 1.8–1.9.
